final_message:
.ts` also passes.

**How I worked:** I wrote the test list first (`TEST_LIST.md`), then went through it one item at a time, seeing each new test fail before writing code. I made seven small commits along the way. Three items were already green the moment I wrote them: "stock is not modified", "same-bin picks keep their order" and "first problem from the top". Earlier design choices had already covered them, so those tests just lock the behaviour in. Two other things to know about the process:
- Twice my first draft of an allocation test also depended on the walking order, which didn't exist yet. I changed the bins in those tests so each one checks only its own rule.
- Once I added three tests in a single step instead of one.

**Implementation** (`src/pickList.ts`; the types and error class are unchanged):
- **Parsing:** the code collects every problem along with its line number and throws the earliest one. Throwing straight away would get some cases wrong. For example, if an `ORDER` line is followed only by a malformed line, the order is empty, and that has to be reported at the `ORDER` line even though it's only detected later.
- **Allocation:** it works on copies of the lots, sorted by best-before date with undated lots last and ties broken by bin. Priority orders are served first, then the rest in text order. Repeated SKUs in an order are added up and keep their first position.
- **Walking order:** a stable sort by aisle, then rack (ascending in the 1st, 3rd, … visited aisle and descending in the 2nd, 4th, …), then level.

**Choices where the spec left room:**
- Lowercase letters are allowed in order ids, since the spec just says "letters".
- Tabs count as spaces, and Windows (CRLF) line endings work.
- If an order id is repeated, only that `ORDER` line is reported. Item lines under the duplicate don't cause extra errors.

Only the last commit has the `Co-Authored-By` line; the six before it don't. I can add it to those by rewriting the local history if you want.
